balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Synopsys, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Synopsys, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Synopsys, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Synopsys, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: Design Automation vs Design IP
segmentRevenue.content:
Synopsys reports two segments: Design Automation -- EDA/simulation software used to design and verify chips (and, since the Ansys acquisition closed July 2025, physics-based simulation for the broader system) -- and Design IP -- pre-built, licensable silicon IP blocks (interface, processor cores, security) that chipmakers license rather than design themselves.

For Synopsys, Inc.: Design Automation is now roughly 3x Design IP and the Ansys deal moved most of the step-change in FY2025-FY2026 scale into this line, not the IP line -- watch that the jump is Ansys integration, not organic EDA acceleration, when comparing growth rates to pre-deal years.

What to watch:

  • Design IP growth, which is lumpier (tied to design-win timing and the semiconductor capex cycle) than the ratable Design Automation line
  • Combined segment margin once Ansys integration costs roll off

licenseMix.title: License revenue recognition: time-based vs upfront
licenseMix.content:
Software license revenue is recognised either ratably over the contract term (time-based) or in full at delivery (upfront), per the contract's accounting treatment -- this split covers product (license) revenue only, not maintenance or professional services.

For Synopsys, Inc.: upfront revenue has grown faster than time-based in recent periods, so reported revenue growth partly reflects a recognition-timing shift, not just more business written -- a rising upfront share pulls future revenue forward and makes one quarter's growth look stronger than the underlying bookings trend.

What to watch:

  • Upfront share rising faster than time-based (timing pull-forward, not necessarily more demand)
  • Deferred revenue and backlog as the check on whether bookings are keeping pace with what is being recognised

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Synopsys, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
